title: Robert M. Shive v. Central Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC left the guilt judgments intact and rejected the requested reversals based on reconciliation, recusal, prosecutorial participation, and alleged Presbytery errors. It reversed the censure of excommunication and remanded for the Session to impose indefinite suspension from the Sacraments, with appropriate conditions pending satisfactory evidence of repentance.
first_summary: Dr. Shive appealed his convictions and excommunication, asserting procedural errors and excessive censure. The SJC rejected the procedural grounds, affirmed the findings of disciplinable offenses, reversed excommunication because the record did not establish contumacy or impenitence, and remanded for indefinite suspension from the Sacraments until satisfactory evidence of repentance.
summary: A church member appealed convictions and excommunication arising from vulgar statements to two patients, challenging the lack of pretrial reconciliation, recusals, the prosecutor’s participation in deliberations, and Presbytery procedure. The SJC left guilt intact and denied a new trial, though it held that a prosecutor may not deliberate as a judge. It reversed excommunication because the record did not show impenitence or contumacy, which could not be inferred from exercising the right to remain silent. It remanded only to impose indefinite suspension from the Sacraments and conditions pending satisfactory evidence of repentance.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The appeal and parties are identified at printed p. 134, lines 14–16; authorship, concurrence, and SJC approval appear at printed p. 143, lines 306–310.
evidence_notes.dispute: The Session’s convictions and excommunication, Presbytery’s affirmance, and the five appellate issues appear at printed pp. 136–137, lines 42–63.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The judgments are stated at printed p. 137, lines 64–74. The prosecutor’s dual role was erroneous but did not justify a new trial (printed pp. 140–141, lines 187–232). Excommunication lacked record support for contumacy or impenitence, and remand required indefinite suspension (printed pp. 142–143, lines 280–300).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The convictions remained in force; only the censure was changed. Silence under BCO 35-1 could not establish contumacy (printed p. 143, lines 292–296). The vote recorded three dissents, but no dissenting opinion is supplied (lines 306–310).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference.

source_limits: The supplied source contains the SJC opinion and vote but no separate dissenting opinion.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the discipline and each category of appellate challenge.
score_reasons.decision: States that guilt remained intact, procedural relief was denied, excommunication was reversed, and remand required indefinite suspension.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains that excommunication lacked evidence of impenitence or contumacy and that protected silence could not supply it.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves both the prosecutor-as-judge rule and the distinction between reversible error and harmless error.
score_reasons.fidelity: Separates the lower-court convictions from the SJC’s rulings and does not treat procedural error as requiring a new trial.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only facts needed to understand the mixed result and practical relief.

verification_notes: Rechecked all five judgments and the operative remand. The final summary clarifies that prosecutor participation was error despite denial of a new trial, that guilt remained intact, and that the remand was limited to imposing indefinite suspension and related conditions.
